title: Pursuit of Second Degree at Local Universities
what_it_is: Pursuit of Second Degree at Local Universities

sections.label: Second local university degree subsidies
sections.summary: Singaporeans may pursue a second local university degree but will not receive tuition subsidies if already subsidised for their first degree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked 	the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) given the Government's push for Singaporeans to re-skill and re-train, whether those who have already obtained a degree from a local university will be able to pursue a second degree in our local university, in a field of study that may be more relevant and in demand in view of disruption and skill obsolescence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: However, he will not receive tuition subsidies if he has already received Government subsidies or sponsorship for his first degree.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: This is because budget and resources are limited and we have to prioritise Government subsidies for those pursuing their first degree.

sections.label: MOE/SSG-supported training places 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, the AUs offered 29,500 MOE/SSG-supported training places, with Singaporeans enjoying subsidies of up to 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: In 2016, the AUs offered 29,500 MOE/SSG-supported training places.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: Singaporeans taking these courses enjoy heavy subsidies, up to 90%.

sections.label: Professional Conversion Programmes for mid-career workers
sections.summary: PCPs help working adults enter new occupations through intensive training and industry attachments, with course fee subsidies, salary support and training allowances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: Another initiative for mid-career Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians would be the Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: PCPs help working adults enter new occupations by providing them with intensive training and industry attachments in a wide range of areas of growth, such as healthcare logistics, and infocomm technology.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: Financial support in the form of course fee subsidies, salary support and training allowances is available under the PCPs.
